cx.doc: Light source x, as a fraction of canvas width; may lie outside the frame

cy.doc: Light source y, as a fraction of canvas height; defaults to the top edge (a skylight); may lie outside the frame

threshold.doc: Bright-pass threshold: only pixels whose premultiplied RGB max component m (0..1) exceeds it glow, with weight (m − t)/(1 − t)

length.doc: Shaft length: the fraction each pixel traces back toward the light source; larger values give longer shafts

intensity.doc: Multiple of the shafts added back onto the source image (additive); 0 = no change

decay.doc: Decay: the further along the shaft, the darker; the furthest point has weight 1 − decay; 0 = the whole shaft is equally bright

tint.doc: Shaft tint, set as a colour string (for gold light, use "#ffd98a"); RGB and alpha multiply the shafts; defaults to white

doc: Volumetric light / god rays: ① bright-pass: premultiplied RGB max component m, per-pixel weight w = clamp((m − threshold)/(1 − threshold), 0, 1), with a 2×2 average down to half resolution; ② radial sampling centred on the light source (cx·W, cy·H), using the same three-pass log-step zoom as filter.radialBlur (8 per pass, σ = −ln(1 − length)), with weights attenuated by (1 − decay)^{o/σ} and normalized per pass; ③ bilinear upsample back to full resolution, with RGB × tint.rgb × intensity and alpha × tint.a × intensity added onto the source, result clamped to alpha ≥ RGB. A pixel receives light from the bright parts along the “pixel → light source” line, so bright objects drag shafts away from the light. f32 arithmetic; transcendental functions are used only through libm to precompute the weight table before the pixel loop. intensity = 0 or length = 0 is byte-identical to the source; bright parts are attached to the full-frame Group, so shafts are not clipped by other element boxes.
